chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever practices medicine or veterinary medicine, let him take the waiver (of liability) from his guardian, otherwise he is responsible for him.'

key_terms.تَبَيْطَرَ: practiced veterinary medicine / was a vet

ai.seo_question: What is the legal liability of a doctor or veterinarian in Shia jurisprudence if they do not obtain a waiver from the patient?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of contractual liability (daman) for medical and veterinary practitioners, requiring them to secure a waiver of liability (bara'ah) from the patient or their guardian before treatment. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the shift from mere professional duty to explicit financial accountability for errors or death, reflecting the broader legal concept of 'guarantee' (daman) in transactions. It highlights the importance of informed consent and clear agreement on risk allocation in early Islamic medical practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said;
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who treats people (doctor) or treats animals (vet), so let him take the waiver from his guardian, or else he would be held responsible for him’.
